agentCan: Build the key-entry connect form and the Basic Auth API plumbing against the correct regional base URL

approval.cost: No developer/app program cost is stated in the docs read (Mailgun account pricing is outside the API documentation pages read)
approval.trigger: No review exists, because there is no app program to review. No app submission, approval queue, or listing/marketplace program for API access appears anywhere in the documentation read. There are no pre-approval user/install caps: each user's key simply works on that user's own account.

blockers.detail: There is no OAuth app object, no client registration, no client_id/client_secret, no authorize endpoint, no consent screen, and no scopes in Mailgun's official documentation. A site search of documentation.mailgun.com for 'client_id' / 'client_secret' / 'authorization code' returns no results at all. Onboarding is 'ask the user to copy a long-lived, full-power credential out of their dashboard and paste it into your product': there is no way for a user to grant limited, revocable-per-app access, because per-app grants don't exist.
blockers.howToClear: No OAuth clearance exists. Use the least-privilege credential available (a Domain Sending Key if you only send), and be transparent with users about what the key can do.
blockers.title: The missing consent flow is the blocker

sources.label: Authentication (Basic Auth, the two API key types, shown-once warning)
Quickstart (account/API-key setup, sandbox authorized recipients, 'under two minutes' claim)

tested: Read-only verification: the authentication model and the ABSENCE of any OAuth program were checked against documentation.mailgun.com, including a site search for 'OAuth' (returns only the InboxReady Slack-alert endpoints, where Mailgun is the OAuth client of Slack) and for 'client_id' / 'client_secret' / 'authorization code' (no results). No account created, nothing submitted.
unverified: Whether any partner/integration program exists outside documentation.mailgun.com (e.g. on mailgun.com marketing pages): out of scope for this pass; within the official API documentation there is none.
API key expiry/rotation policy: no lifetime is stated for either key type in the docs read.
Any limit on the number of Domain Sending Keys per domain or API keys per account (not stated).

alternatives: Primary account API key ('Private API key' in the dashboard; generated automatically at signup; 'allows you to perform all CRUD operations via our various API endpoints and for any of your sending domains'; all-or-nothing, no scopes)
flavor.recommended: No OAuth flavor exists. The least-bad documented pattern: a Domain Sending Key per domain if your product only needs to send as the user
flavor.why: There is no app object. The credential objects are API keys of two documented types, and authentication on every call is HTTP Basic Auth, username 'api', password = the API key, against the regional base URL (api.mailgun.net US / api.eu.mailgun.net EU). A Domain Sending Key 'only allows sending messages via a POST call on /messages and /messages.mime endpoints for the domain in which they are created for': it is the least-privilege credential Mailgun offers. If your product needs full API access, the user must paste their primary account API key, which grants full CRUD over the whole account and all its sending domains.

humanMust: Each user retrieves their own key from their own Mailgun dashboard (Account Settings > API Keys) and pastes it into your product
For a Domain Sending Key: the user creates it under Sending > Domains > Domain Settings > Sending API keys and copies it immediately (it cannot be shown again)
Sandbox sends: each recipient must be added as an authorized recipient and click the verification link before mail can be sent to them
name: Mailgun
nuances: Keys are shown once: a Domain Sending Key cannot be displayed again after creation; losing it means creating a new one and updating every place the old one was pasted.
Region matters: domains live in the US or EU region and calls must go to the matching base URL, a detail the user (not a consent screen) has to get right when connecting.
The Quickstart's only duration claim is 'Send an email in under two minutes' using the sandbox domain; no API key lifetime/expiry figure is stated for either key type.

The word 'OAuth' in Mailgun's docs refers to Mailgun consuming OTHER services (a Slack connection for InboxReady alerts, revoked via DELETE /v1/alerts/slack/oauth), not to third parties authorizing against Mailgun. Don't mistake those endpoints for a developer OAuth program.
prerequisites: A key-entry connect form and secure credential storage in your product
Regional base URL handling (US and EU)

steps.detail: The user signs in to Mailgun, opens Account Settings > API Keys, and clicks the eye icon next to the Private API key. This key allows all CRUD operations for any of the user's sending domains.
steps.title: (Full access) User retrieves the primary account API key

steps.detail: Dashboard > Sending tab > Domains > select the domain > Domain Settings > Sending API keys tab > Add Sending Key, give it a description, Create Sending Key, then copy it immediately: 'For security purposes, we will not be able to show you the key again. If you lose your key, you will need to create a new key.' The key only allows sending via POST /messages and /messages.mime for that domain.
steps.title: (Least privilege, send-only) User creates a Domain Sending Key

steps.detail: The user pastes the key into your product; you store it and call the API with HTTP Basic Auth (--user 'api:YOUR_API_KEY') against the correct regional base URL for the user's domain (api.mailgun.net US / api.eu.mailgun.net EU). On the sandbox domain, each recipient must first be an authorized recipient who clicked the verification link.
steps.title: Store the key; call the API

tagline: Mailgun has no OAuth program for third-party apps at all: no app object, no client registration, no consent screen. The only documented connection is a user pasting an API key, the full-power primary key or a send-only Domain Sending Key.

time.active: Minutes: a key-entry form plus Basic Auth plumbing
time.total: Same day; there is no program to be approved by
